---
title: "Orting maps and story layers in the site style"
jupyter: python3
---

Everything here writes to `figures/`. Run the chunks in order; each one stands on its own.

## 1. Orting REM and change maps (Orting Study page)

```{python}
import numpy as np, rasterio, logging
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, matplotlib.patheffects as pe
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, to_rgb
from rasterio.enums import Resampling
from scipy import ndimage
from pyproj import Transformer
from PIL import Image
logging.getLogger("matplotlib.font_manager").setLevel(logging.ERROR)

D = "data/processed/"
K2 = 2                     # read every 2 m (plenty for a web figure)
CELL = 1.0 * K2
def rd(name):
    with rasterio.open(D + name) as s:
        a = s.read(1, out_shape=(s.height // K2, s.width // K2), resampling=Resampling.average).astype("float32")
        b = s.bounds
    return a, (b.left, b.right, b.bottom, b.top)

rem, ext = rd("rem_2020_1m.tif")
dod, _ = rd("dod_2011_2020.tif")
dtm, _ = rd("dtm_2020_1m.tif")
inside = np.isfinite(dtm)

BG, TEXT, SUB = "#081b2c", "#e8f3f6", "#9dbfcc"
stops = ["#f7fcfd", "#d3ecf2", "#86c1d1", "#2e7594", "#123d5d", "#081b2c"]
deep = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("deep", stops)
SERIF = ["Lora", "Georgia", "DejaVu Serif"]; SANS = ["Inter", "Segoe UI", "DejaVu Sans"]
halo = [pe.withStroke(linewidth=3, foreground=BG, alpha=0.6)]
to_sp = Transformer.from_crs(4326, 2856, always_xy=True)

def hillshade(z, azdeg=315, altdeg=35, vex=3.0):
    z = np.where(np.isfinite(z), z, np.nanmedian(z))
    gy, gx = np.gradient(z * vex, -CELL, CELL)
    az, alt = np.radians(90 - azdeg), np.radians(altdeg)
    lx, ly, lz = np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(alt)
    hs = (-gx * lx - gy * ly + lz) / np.sqrt(gx * gx + gy * gy + 1)
    lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(hs[inside], [0.5, 99.5])
    return np.clip((hs - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1).astype("float32")

hs = 0.75 * hillshade(dtm, 315, 35) + 0.25 * hillshade(dtm, 225, 50)

FADE_M = 100.0   # width of the soft edge, in metres

def finish(rgb, path, legend):
    # outside the study area is see-through, with a wide soft fade, so the map sits on the page's terrain background
    # fade by distance from the study-area edge: fully see-through AT the edge, fully solid FADE_M inside
    # pad with a ring of "outside" so the fade also reaches zero where the study area touches the raster's edge
    dist = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(np.pad(inside, 1))[1:-1, 1:-1] * CELL   # metres to the nearest outside cell
    fade = np.clip(dist / FADE_M, 0, 1)
    fade = fade * fade * (3 - 2 * fade)                       # smoothstep: eases in and out, no visible line
    rgba = np.dstack([np.clip(np.nan_to_num(rgb), 0, 1), fade])
    # shrink to the final size with Pillow, which handles see-through edges correctly
    # ("RGBa" = premultiplied alpha, so faded edges don't pick up a white halo)
    h, w = rgba.shape[:2]
    W_OUT = 1200; H_OUT = round(W_OUT * h / w)
    im = Image.fromarray((rgba * 255).round().astype("uint8"), "RGBA").convert("RGBa")
    im = np.asarray(im.resize((W_OUT, H_OUT), Image.LANCZOS).convert("RGBA"))
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W_OUT / 200, H_OUT / 200), facecolor="none")
    ax = fig.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1]); ax.imshow(im, extent=ext, interpolation="none"); ax.axis("off")
    x, y = to_sp.transform(-122.204, 47.098)
    ax.text(x, y, "ORTING", color=TEXT, fontsize=12, fontfamily=SANS, ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo)
    for name, fx, fy, rot in [("Puyallup River", 0.38, 0.64, 68), ("Carbon River", 0.76, 0.42, -42)]:
        x, y = ext[0] + fx * (ext[1] - ext[0]), ext[3] - fy * (ext[3] - ext[2])
        ax.text(x, y, name, color=TEXT, fontsize=12, fontfamily=SERIF, style="italic", rotation=rot,
                ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo)
    legend(fig)
    # 1 km scale bar
    sx, sy = ext[0] + 0.06 * (ext[1] - ext[0]), ext[2] + 0.035 * (ext[3] - ext[2])
    ax.plot([sx, sx + 1000], [sy, sy], color=SUB, lw=2)
    ax.text(sx + 500, sy + 150, "1 km", color=SUB, fontsize=10, fontfamily=SANS, ha="center")
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=200, transparent=True); plt.close(fig)

# ---- REM map --------------------------------------------------------------
RMAX = 6.0
t = (np.clip(np.nan_to_num(rem, nan=RMAX), 0, RMAX) / RMAX) ** 0.5   # 0 = river, 1 = 6 m or more; the square root stretches the low end
low = t < 1
rgb = deep(t)[..., :3].astype("float32")
edge = ndimage.gaussian_filter(low.astype("float32"), 6)
strength = 0.70 - 0.30 * edge
rgb *= (1 - strength * (1 - hs))[..., None]
sun = np.clip(hs - 0.55, 0, None) * 0.16 * (1 - 0.6 * edge)
rgb += sun[..., None] * np.array(to_rgb(stops[2]))
glow = ndimage.gaussian_filter((1 - t) * low, 12)
rgb = 1 - (1 - rgb) * (1 - 0.25 * glow[..., None] * np.array(to_rgb(stops[1])))

def rem_legend(fig):
    lax = fig.add_axes([0.07, 0.10, 0.03, 0.13])
    lax.imshow(np.linspace(1, 0, 256)[:, None] ** 0.5, cmap=deep, aspect="auto"); lax.axis("off")
    fig.text(0.115, 0.225, "6 m or more above the river", color=SUB, fontsize=10.5, fontfamily=SANS, va="center")
    fig.text(0.115, 0.105, "River level or below", color=SUB, fontsize=10.5, fontfamily=SANS, va="center")
finish(rgb, "figures/rem_map.png", rem_legend)

# ---- change map -----------------------------------------------------------
LOD, CMAX = 0.23, 1.5
ERODE, DEPOSIT = np.array(to_rgb("#ff6b5b")), np.array(to_rgb("#5cc8f0"))
base = np.array(to_rgb("#081b2c")) + (np.array(to_rgb("#1d3d54")) - np.array(to_rgb("#081b2c"))) * hs[..., None]
d = np.nan_to_num(dod, nan=0.0)
a = np.clip((np.abs(d) - LOD) / (CMAX - LOD), 0, 1) ** 0.7
a = np.where(np.abs(d) < LOD, 0, 0.35 + 0.65 * a)[..., None]
col = np.where((d < 0)[..., None], ERODE, DEPOSIT)
rgb = base * (1 - a) + col * a
glow_e = ndimage.gaussian_filter((a[..., 0] * (d < 0)).astype("float32"), 4)
glow_d = ndimage.gaussian_filter((a[..., 0] * (d > 0)).astype("float32"), 4)
rgb = 1 - (1 - rgb) * (1 - 0.35 * glow_e[..., None] * ERODE) * (1 - 0.35 * glow_d[..., None] * DEPOSIT)

def dod_legend(fig):
    lax = fig.add_axes([0.07, 0.10, 0.03, 0.13])
    ramp = np.concatenate([np.tile(DEPOSIT, (128, 1)) * np.linspace(1, 0.35, 128)[:, None],
                           np.tile(ERODE, (128, 1)) * np.linspace(0.35, 1, 128)[:, None]])
    lax.imshow(ramp[:, None, :], aspect="auto"); lax.axis("off")
    fig.text(0.115, 0.225, "Deposition (ground built up)", color=SUB, fontsize=10.5, fontfamily=SANS, va="center")
    fig.text(0.115, 0.105, "Erosion (ground lowered)", color=SUB, fontsize=10.5, fontfamily=SANS, va="center")
finish(rgb, "figures/change_map.png", dod_legend)
```

## 2. Change layer for the story (sits on the valley map)

```{python}
# ---- story overlay: Orting change layer, in the valley map's coordinates (UTM 10N) ----
import numpy as np, rasterio
from rasterio.enums import Resampling
from rasterio.warp import reproject, calculate_default_transform
from matplotlib.colors import to_rgb
from scipy import ndimage
from PIL import Image

D = "data/processed/"
with rasterio.open(D + "dod_2011_2020.tif") as s:
    k = 2                                                     # 2 m cells
    dod = s.read(1, out_shape=(s.height // k, s.width // k), resampling=Resampling.average).astype("float32")
    src_t = s.transform * s.transform.scale(s.width / dod.shape[1], s.height / dod.shape[0])
    src_crs, b = s.crs, s.bounds
with rasterio.open(D + "dtm_2020_1m.tif") as s:
    inside = np.isfinite(s.read(1, out_shape=dod.shape, resampling=Resampling.average))

# colors: a dark wash over the study area so the change stands out, then erosion / deposition on top
LOD, CMAX = 0.23, 1.5
ERODE, DEPOSIT, WASH = np.array(to_rgb("#ff6b5b")), np.array(to_rgb("#5cc8f0")), np.array(to_rgb("#06213a"))
d = np.nan_to_num(dod, nan=0.0)
a = np.clip((np.abs(d) - LOD) / (CMAX - LOD), 0, 1) ** 0.7
a = np.where(np.abs(d) < LOD, 0, 0.45 + 0.55 * a)
col = np.where((d < 0)[..., None], ERODE, DEPOSIT)
dist = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(np.pad(inside, 1))[1:-1, 1:-1] * k    # metres to the edge (padded so raster borders count)
edge = np.clip(dist / 300.0, 0, 1)                                          # 0 at the study-area edge, 1 at 300 m in
edge = edge * edge * (3 - 2 * edge)                                         # smoothstep
# two layers, so the story can fade the wash in first and then reveal the change on top of it
wash = np.dstack([np.broadcast_to(WASH, col.shape), 0.70 * edge]).astype("float32")
lines = np.dstack([col, a * edge]).astype("float32")

# reproject both to UTM 10N (the valley map's system) on a 3 m grid
dst_t, w, h = calculate_default_transform(src_crs, 26910, dod.shape[1], dod.shape[0], *b, resolution=3.0)
for layer, name in [(wash, "orting_change_wash.webp"), (lines, "orting_change_lines.webp")]:
    out = np.zeros((4, h, w), dtype="float32")
    for i in range(4):
        reproject(np.ascontiguousarray(layer[..., i]), out[i], src_transform=src_t, src_crs=src_crs,
                  dst_transform=dst_t, dst_crs=26910, resampling=Resampling.bilinear,
                  src_nodata=None, dst_nodata=0)
    img = (np.clip(np.moveaxis(out, 0, -1), 0, 1) * 255).round().astype("uint8")
    Image.fromarray(img, "RGBA").save("figures/" + name, quality=85, method=6)

# where both layers sit on the valley map, as percentages (these go in story.qmd)
X0, X1, Y0, Y1 = 541000, 565000, 5210000, 5238000
left, top = dst_t.c, dst_t.f
right, bottom = left + w * dst_t.a, top + h * dst_t.e
print(f"left: {(left - X0) / (X1 - X0) * 100:.3f}%; top: {(Y1 - top) / (Y1 - Y0) * 100:.3f}%; "
      f"width: {(right - left) / (X1 - X0) * 100:.3f}%; height: {(top - bottom) / (Y1 - Y0) * 100:.3f}%;")
```

## 3. Site background (lidar plateau north of the valley)

```{python}
# site background: lidar hillshade of the plateau north of the valley, shaded like the map's uplands
import numpy as np, rasterio
from rasterio.windows import from_bounds
from matplotlib.colors import to_rgb
from PIL import Image

CELL = 3.0
BG, LIFT_C = np.array(to_rgb("#081b2c")), np.array(to_rgb("#86c1d1"))
def hillshade(z, azdeg, altdeg, vex=4.0):
    gy, gx = np.gradient(z * np.float32(vex), np.float32(-CELL), np.float32(CELL))
    az, alt = np.radians(90 - azdeg), np.radians(altdeg)
    lx, ly, lz = np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(alt)
    hs = (-gx * lx - gy * ly + lz) / np.sqrt(gx * gx + gy * gy + 1)
    lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(hs, [0.1, 99.9])
    return np.clip((hs - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1).astype("float32")

x0, y0, w_px, h_px = 550000, 5229000, 2560, 1600          # 7.7 x 4.8 km, one pixel per 3 m cell
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_dem_3m_filled.tif") as s:
    win = from_bounds(x0, y0, x0 + w_px * CELL, y0 + h_px * CELL, s.transform)
    z = s.read(1, window=win).astype("float32")
z = np.where(np.isfinite(z), z, np.nanmedian(z))
hs = 0.75 * hillshade(z, 315, 35) + 0.25 * hillshade(z, 225, 50)
rgb = BG * (1 - 0.70 * (1 - hs))[..., None]                                 # shaded dark base
rgb = rgb + (np.clip(hs - 0.55, 0, None) * 0.16)[..., None] * LIFT_C        # sunlit slopes lifted in teal
Image.fromarray((np.clip(rgb, 0, 1) * 255).round().astype("uint8")).save("figures/bg_terrain.jpg", quality=88)
```

## 4. Real terrain around the valley map (moves with the story map)

```{python}
# terrain around the valley map, so the story's background is the real landscape and moves with the map
import numpy as np, rasterio
from rasterio.warp import reproject, Resampling
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from matplotlib.colors import to_rgb
from scipy import ndimage
from PIL import Image

CELL = 10.0
X0, X1, Y0, Y1 = 515000, 575000, 5206000, 5246000          # 60 x 40 km around the valley map
W, H = int((X1 - X0) / CELL), int((Y1 - Y0) / CELL)
dst_t = from_origin(X0, Y1, CELL, CELL)
z = np.full((H, W), np.nan, dtype="float32")
with rasterio.open("data/raw/usgs_ned_13/USGS_13_n48w123.tif") as src:
    reproject(rasterio.band(src, 1), z, src_nodata=src.nodata, dst_transform=dst_t, dst_crs=26910,
              dst_nodata=np.nan, resampling=Resampling.bilinear)
water = ~np.isfinite(z) | (z < 0.5)
z = np.where(np.isfinite(z), z, 0)

def hillshade(z, azdeg, altdeg, vex=4.0):
    gy, gx = np.gradient(z * np.float32(vex), np.float32(-CELL), np.float32(CELL))
    az, alt = np.radians(90 - azdeg), np.radians(altdeg)
    lx, ly, lz = np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt), np.sin(alt)
    hs = (-gx * lx - gy * ly + lz) / np.sqrt(gx * gx + gy * gy + 1)
    lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(hs[~water], [0.1, 99.9])
    return np.clip((hs - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1).astype("float32")

hs = 0.75 * hillshade(z, 315, 35) + 0.25 * hillshade(z, 225, 50)
BG, LIFT_C, SEA = np.array(to_rgb("#081b2c")), np.array(to_rgb("#86c1d1")), np.array(to_rgb("#0c2538"))
rgb = BG * (1 - 0.70 * (1 - hs))[..., None]                                   # same recipe as the map's uplands
rgb = rgb + (np.clip(hs - 0.55, 0, None) * 0.16)[..., None] * LIFT_C
sea = ndimage.gaussian_filter(water.astype("float32"), 2)[..., None]          # soft shoreline
rgb = rgb * (1 - sea) + SEA * sea
Image.fromarray((np.clip(rgb, 0, 1) * 255).round().astype("uint8")).save("figures/story_skirt.jpg", quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True)

# where the skirt sits relative to the valley map (541-565 km E, 5210-5238 km N), for story.qmd
MX0, MX1, MY0, MY1 = 541000, 565000, 5210000, 5238000
mw, mh = MX1 - MX0, MY1 - MY0
print(f"top: {-(Y1 - MY1) / mh * 100:.3f}%; right: {-(X1 - MX1) / mw * 100:.3f}%; "
      f"bottom: {-(MY0 - Y0) / mh * 100:.3f}%; left: {-(MX0 - X0) / mw * 100:.3f}%;")
```

## 5. Story map with its edges blended into the terrain (keeps the camera moves sharp)

```{python}
# story map with its edges blended into the surrounding terrain, so the page needs no CSS mask
# (a masked image can't be drawn at full resolution while it moves, which made the camera moves blocky)
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
story = Image.open("figures/valley_story.jpg").convert("RGB")       # 541-565 km E, 5210-5238 km N
skirt = Image.open("figures/story_skirt.jpg").convert("RGB")       # 515-575 km E, 5206-5246 km N, 10 m pixels
W, H = story.size
under = skirt.crop(((541000 - 515000) // 10, (5246000 - 5238000) // 10,
                    (565000 - 515000) // 10, (5246000 - 5210000) // 10)).resize((W, H), Image.BICUBIC)
# same fade as the old CSS mask: 0 at the edge, full strength 5% in (sides) and 4% in (top and bottom)
fx = np.interp(np.minimum(np.arange(W), W - 1 - np.arange(W)) / W, [0, .015, .03, .05], [0, .35, .75, 1])
fy = np.interp(np.minimum(np.arange(H), H - 1 - np.arange(H)) / H, [0, .012, .025, .04], [0, .35, .75, 1])
w = (fy[:, None] * fx[None, :])[..., None]
out = np.asarray(story, dtype="float32") * w + np.asarray(under, dtype="float32") * (1 - w)
Image.fromarray(out.round().astype("uint8")).save("figures/valley_story_edge.jpg", quality=88, optimize=True, progressive=True)
```

## 6. Delta fan highlight for the Commencement Bay stop

```{python}
# delta fan highlight for the story's Commencement Bay stop (sits on the valley map like the change layers)
import numpy as np, rasterio
from scipy import ndimage
from matplotlib.path import Path
from PIL import Image

with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_seafloor_3m.tif") as s:
    z = s.read(1)                                    # same 3 m grid as the valley map
H, W = z.shape
sea = np.isfinite(z)
lab, _ = ndimage.label(sea); size = np.bincount(lab.ravel()); size[0] = 0
sea = lab == size.argmax()                           # the open bay and its waterways

# the fan as sketched over the map (fractions of the map across, down), trimmed by depth below
outline = [(.0042,.0761),(.0219,.0651),(.0416,.0482),(.0613,.0347),(.0869,.0263),(.1105,.0162),(.1283,.0094),
           (.1440,.0145),(.1578,.0280),(.1696,.0449),(.1578,.0432),(.1480,.0449),(.1401,.0533),(.1362,.0601),
           (.1293,.0601),(.1263,.0668),(.1204,.0803),(.1165,.0938),(.1066,.0989),(.0987,.1040),(.0908,.1023),
           (.0869,.1107),(.0751,.1209),(.0653,.1259),(.0515,.1141),(.0357,.1006),(.0180,.0871),(.0081,.0786)]
C0, R0, C1, R1 = 0, 0, 1600, 1400                    # work in the bay corner only
rr, cc = np.mgrid[R0:R1, C0:C1]
inside = Path([(u * W, v * H) for u, v in outline]).contains_points(np.c_[cc.ravel(), rr.ravel()]).reshape(rr.shape)
fan = inside & sea[R0:R1, C0:C1] & (np.nan_to_num(z[R0:R1, C0:C1], nan=-999) > -100)   # delta top and front, above the deep basin
fan = ndimage.gaussian_filter(fan.astype("float32"), 6) > .5                            # smooth the edge

SAND = np.array([205, 184, 255]) / 255                   # pale violet, so it reads apart from the gold port layer
soft = ndimage.gaussian_filter(fan.astype("float32"), 3)
edge = np.clip(ndimage.gaussian_filter((ndimage.binary_dilation(fan, iterations=2) & ~ndimage.binary_erosion(fan, iterations=2)).astype("float32"), 2.5) * 2.2, 0, 1)
alpha = np.clip(0.16 * soft + 0.9 * edge, 0, 1)
rgba = np.dstack([np.broadcast_to(SAND, alpha.shape + (3,)), alpha])
Image.fromarray((rgba * 255).round().astype("uint8"), "RGBA").save("figures/bay_delta.webp", quality=90, method=6)
print(f"left: 0%; top: 0%; width: {C1 / W * 100:.3f}%; height: {R1 / H * 100:.3f}%;  fan area {fan.sum() * 9 / 1e6:.2f} km2")
```

## 7. Port of Tacoma today (downloads the outline from Pierce County, draws the port as a raster layer)

```{python}
# Port of Tacoma today: Pierce County's port industrial area, shown as a raster layer on the valley map
# (like the Orting change layer: the port's own ground from the 3 m DEM, tinted so it stands apart)
# downloads the outline once from Pierce County's ArcGIS service, then reuses the saved copy
from pathlib import Path
import requests, numpy as np, geopandas as gpd, rasterio
from rasterio import features
from rasterio.windows import Window
from scipy import ndimage
from PIL import Image

out = Path("data/reach/port_of_tacoma.geojson")
if not out.exists():
    url = ("https://services2.arcgis.com/1UvBaQ5y1ubjUPmd/ArcGIS/rest/services/Ports/FeatureServer/0/query"
           "?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson")
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
    r.raise_for_status()
    out.write_text(r.text)
port = gpd.read_file(out).to_crs(26910)
print(f"{len(port)} feature(s), {port.area.sum() / 1e6:.2f} km2, bounds {port.total_bounds.round()}")

# the bay corner of the 3 m valley grid (top left 541 000 E, 5 238 000 N), the same grid as the story map
C1, R1 = 3000, 2240
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_dem_3m_filled.tif") as s:
    z = s.read(1, window=Window(0, 0, C1, R1)).astype("float32")
    tf = s.window_transform(Window(0, 0, C1, R1))
inside = features.rasterize(((g, 1) for g in port.geometry), out_shape=(R1, C1), transform=tf).astype(bool)
z = np.where(np.isfinite(z), z, 0)

# texture: hillshade of the port's own ground, so terminals, fill and waterways show through the tint
gy, gx = np.gradient(z * 8.0, -3.0, 3.0)
az, alt = np.radians(90 - 315), np.radians(35)
hs = (-gx * np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt) - gy * np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt) + np.sin(alt)) / np.sqrt(gx**2 + gy**2 + 1)
lo, hi = np.percentile(hs[inside], [1, 99]); hs = np.clip((hs - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1)
height = np.clip(z / 8.0, 0, 1)                                  # 0 m (water) to 8 m (highest fill)
DARK, LIGHT = np.array([0.55, 0.33, 0.12]), np.array([1.0, 0.86, 0.60])   # bronze to pale gold
t = (0.10 + 0.35 * height + 0.55 * hs)[..., None]          # mostly relief, some height
rgb = DARK + (LIGHT - DARK) * t

water = z < 0.5
soft = ndimage.gaussian_filter(inside.astype("float32"), 2)
edge = (ndimage.binary_dilation(inside, iterations=2) & ~ndimage.binary_erosion(inside, iterations=2)).astype("float32")
alpha = soft * np.where(water, 0.22, 0.58)                        # land tinted, waterways lightly; the map shows through
alpha = np.clip(alpha + np.clip(ndimage.gaussian_filter(edge, 2) * 2.2, 0, 1) * 0.9, 0, 1)
rgb = np.where(edge[..., None] > 0, LIGHT, rgb)
rgba = np.dstack([rgb, alpha])
Image.fromarray((np.clip(rgba, 0, 1) * 255).round().astype("uint8"), "RGBA").save("figures/port_overlay.webp", quality=88, method=6)
print("saved figures/port_overlay.webp")
```

## 8. Orting today (downloads the city limits from Pierce County, draws the town as a raster layer)

```{python}
# Orting today: the city limits from Pierce County, shown as a raster layer on the valley map
# (like the port layer: the town's own ground from the 3 m DEM, tinted green so it stands apart)
# downloads Pierce County's city boundaries once, then reuses the saved copy
from pathlib import Path
import requests, numpy as np, geopandas as gpd, rasterio
from rasterio import features
from rasterio.windows import Window
from scipy import ndimage
from PIL import Image

out = Path("data/reach/pierce_cities.geojson")
if not out.exists():
    url = ("https://services2.arcgis.com/1UvBaQ5y1ubjUPmd/ArcGIS/rest/services/Cities_in_Pierce_County/FeatureServer/0/query"
           "?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson")
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
    r.raise_for_status()
    out.write_text(r.text)
cities = gpd.read_file(out).to_crs(26910)
# pick Orting by name, whatever the name column is called
is_orting = np.zeros(len(cities), bool)
for c in cities.columns.drop("geometry"):
    is_orting |= cities[c].astype(str).str.strip().str.lower().eq("orting").to_numpy()
orting = cities[is_orting]
if orting.empty:
    raise SystemExit(f"Orting not found; the columns are {list(cities.columns)}")
print(f"{len(cities)} cities; Orting: {len(orting)} feature(s), {orting.area.sum() / 1e6:.2f} km2, bounds {orting.total_bounds.round()}")

# a fixed 6.3 x 6.3 km window of the 3 m valley grid around Orting (cols 5450-7550, rows 6100-8200)
C0, R0, N = 5450, 6100, 2100
with rasterio.open("data/processed/valley_dem_3m_filled.tif") as s:
    z = s.read(1, window=Window(C0, R0, N, N)).astype("float32")
    tf = s.window_transform(Window(C0, R0, N, N))
    print(f"valley grid {s.width} x {s.height}; layer sits at left {C0 / s.width * 100:.3f}%, top {R0 / s.height * 100:.4f}%, "
          f"width {N / s.width * 100:.3f}%, height {N / s.height * 100:.4f}%")
inside = features.rasterize(((g, 1) for g in orting.geometry), out_shape=(N, N), transform=tf).astype(bool)
edge_px = inside[0].any() or inside[-1].any() or inside[:, 0].any() or inside[:, -1].any()
if edge_px: print("note: Orting reaches the edge of the window, so a little of it is cut off")
z = np.where(np.isfinite(z), z, np.nanmedian(z))

# texture: hillshade of the town's own ground (streets, lots, terraces), tinted green
gy, gx = np.gradient(z * 8.0, -3.0, 3.0)
az, alt = np.radians(90 - 315), np.radians(35)
hs = (-gx * np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt) - gy * np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt) + np.sin(alt)) / np.sqrt(gx**2 + gy**2 + 1)
lo, hi = np.percentile(hs[inside], [1, 99]); hs = np.clip((hs - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1)
DARK, LIGHT = np.array([0.20, 0.42, 0.24]), np.array([0.80, 0.96, 0.70])   # deep green to pale green
rgb = DARK + (LIGHT - DARK) * (0.25 + 0.75 * hs)[..., None]

soft = ndimage.gaussian_filter(inside.astype("float32"), 2)
edge = (ndimage.binary_dilation(inside, iterations=2) & ~ndimage.binary_erosion(inside, iterations=2)).astype("float32")
alpha = soft * 0.55                                                      # the map shows through
alpha = np.clip(alpha + np.clip(ndimage.gaussian_filter(edge, 2) * 2.2, 0, 1) * 0.9, 0, 1)
rgb = np.where(edge[..., None] > 0, LIGHT, rgb)
Image.fromarray((np.clip(np.dstack([rgb, alpha]), 0, 1) * 255).round().astype("uint8"), "RGBA").save(
    "figures/orting_overlay.webp", quality=88, method=6)
print("saved figures/orting_overlay.webp")
```

## 9. Pacific today (downloads the city limits from WSDOT, draws the outline only)

```{python}
# Pacific today: the city limits as a thin outline only, so the glowing valley floor stays clear
# Pacific is mostly in King County, so this uses WSDOT's statewide city limits (from the state Office of Financial Management)
from pathlib import Path
import requests, numpy as np, geopandas as gpd
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFilter

out = Path("data/reach/pacific_city_limits.geojson")
if not out.exists():
    base = "https://data.wsdot.wa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Shared/CityLimits/MapServer/2/query"
    r = requests.get(base, params={"where": "CityName = 'Pacific'", "outFields": "*", "outSR": 4326, "f": "geojson"}, timeout=60)
    r.raise_for_status()
    out.write_text(r.text)
pacific = gpd.read_file(out).to_crs(26910)
if pacific.empty:
    out.unlink()
    raise SystemExit("Pacific not found in the download; tell Claude and paste this message")
print(f"Pacific: {len(pacific)} feature(s), {pacific.area.sum() / 1e6:.2f} km2, bounds {pacific.total_bounds.round()}")

# a fixed 6 x 6 km window of the valley map (cols 4300-6300, rows 0-2000 of the 3 m grid), drawn at 1.5 m per pixel
# so the line stays crisp when the story zooms in
X0, Y0, SIZE, PX = 541000 + 4300 * 3, 5238000, 6000, 1.5
NPX = int(SIZE / PX)                                    # 4000 x 4000 pixels
minx, miny, maxx, maxy = pacific.total_bounds
if minx < X0 or maxx > X0 + SIZE or miny < Y0 - SIZE or maxy > Y0:
    print("note: part of Pacific falls outside the window, so the outline is cut off there")
def to_px(coords):
    return [((x - X0) / PX, (Y0 - y) / PX) for x, y in coords]
rings = []
for g in pacific.geometry:
    for poly in getattr(g, "geoms", [g]):
        rings += [poly.exterior] + list(poly.interiors)

# a dark halo under a light line (like the story's pointer lines), so it shows on bright ground too
halo = Image.new("L", (NPX, NPX), 0); line = Image.new("L", (NPX, NPX), 0)
dh, dl = ImageDraw.Draw(halo), ImageDraw.Draw(line)
for ring in rings:
    pts = to_px(ring.coords)
    dh.line(pts, fill=255, width=26, joint="curve")
    dl.line(pts, fill=255, width=12, joint="curve")
halo = halo.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(4)); line = line.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.0))
h = np.asarray(halo, dtype="float32") / 255 * 0.55
l = np.asarray(line, dtype="float32") / 255
alpha = l + h * (1 - l)
col_line, col_halo = np.array([0.95, 0.98, 0.99]), np.array([0.02, 0.10, 0.16])
rgb = (col_line * l[..., None] + col_halo * (h * (1 - l))[..., None]) / np.maximum(alpha, 1e-6)[..., None]
Image.fromarray((np.clip(np.dstack([rgb, alpha]), 0, 1) * 255).round().astype("uint8"), "RGBA").save(
    "figures/pacific_outline.webp", lossless=False, quality=90, method=6)
print("saved figures/pacific_outline.webp; it sits at left 53.75%, top 0%, width 25%, height 21.4293% of the valley map")
```
